title: Developer Fidelity & Cost Negotiator — design note and API contract
author: Asha Patel
summary: This design document defines the Developer Fidelity & Cost Negotiator (DFCN): a product component that mediates per-route and per-tenant fidelity preferences against runtime cost/SLO constraints. DFCN provides an API and UX contract used by the Console, SDKs, and runtime router to recommend, enforce, and simulate fidelity choices with observable cost impact.
background: Teams building on Redwood increasingly want programmatic control over the fidelity/quality vs unit-cost tradeoff: e.g., choose cheaper quantized variants for low-value paths, reserve high-fidelity for critical routes, or allow dynamic fidelity adjustment during bursts. Existing artifacts describe negotiation APIs (2026) and fidelity advisors (2026–2028) but there is no single runtime-facing orchestrator that exposes a deterministic contract for client SDKs, console affordances, and billing reconciliation. DFCN fills that gap.
goals: Provide a single API surface for intent-based fidelity preferences (developer intent, SLOs, cost caps).
Produce deterministic negotiation results and a simulation endpoint for onboarding and cost forecasting.
Ensure the runtime can apply negotiated outcomes with <100ms decision latency at the routing layer for 99th perc. request volume.
Emit telemetry necessary for cost attribution, fidelity regressions, and rollback triggers.
Support a safe rollout path: canary, tenant opt-in, and enterprise override via policy.
Keep billing attribution auditable and compatible with existing crediting and SLA systems.
non_functional_requirements: Decision latency: median <5ms, p99 <50ms for cached policies; cold-path negotiation p99 <100ms.
Availability: 99.95% for negotiation API (aligned with control-plane SLA), graceful degradation to a conservative default policy.
Scalability: support 10k concurrent negotiations per second globally with autoscaling.
Determinism: same input (tenant, route, request-metadata, seed) must always produce same negotiation output when pinned to same policy version.
Observability: every negotiation returns a decision_id that links to structured telemetry and reasoning trace.
acceptance_criteria: API implements v1 contract and passes negative/edge-case tests in simulator harness.
Integration tests demonstrate runtime can apply decisions at router with target latencies under loaded synthetic traffic.
Telemetry pipeline surfaces cost delta per-route and fidelity-change events, and billing matches simulation within 2% on sample tenants.
Security review completed and enterprise policy override path validated with KMS-backed config.
high_level_design:
Overview:

DFCN consists of three logical subsystems: (1) policy compiler (control plane), (2) negotiation engine (stateless microservice), and (3) runtime enforcer.

Policy compiler: ingests templates (tenant-level defaults, route overrides, canary experiments, safety guardrails) and produces a compact policy blob versioned using semantic versioning. Blobs include: fidelity tiers, quantization hints, fallbacks, and credit-cost multipliers.

Negotiation engine: takes inputs (tenant_id, route_id, route_metadata, desired_intent {cost_cap, latency_cap, fidelity_preference}, runtime_hints {kv_cache_hit, session_tokens}, policy_blob_version) and returns a Decision (fidelity_tier, variant_id, cache_hint, estimated_cost_tokens, decision_id, reasoning_trace). Decisions are signed with a control-plane key for audit. A read-through cache stores recent decisions keyed by request fingerprint.

Runtime enforcer: lightweight adapter in the router that consumes the Decision and maps decision fields to execution paths (model variant selection, quantize flag, batch priority). Enforcer falls back to conservative defaults on verification failure.

Data model (flat text table embedded in this doc):

| Field | Type | Description | Example |
|-------|------|-------------|---------|
| decision_id | string | opaque UUID for traceability | dec_01H2X34ABCD |
| fidelity_tier | string | human-friendly tier (low/medium/high/ultra) | medium |
| variant_id | string | model variant to select | rwd-gptx-2q8 |
| estimated_cost_tokens | number | estimated token cost for this request | 0.32 |
| reasoning_trace | string | short structured reason codes | PRIORITY=latency;FALLBACK=quantized
api_contract:
API v1 summary:

POST /v1/negotiations/simulate
- Purpose: dry-run a negotiation for onboarding and billing simulation.
- Body (JSON): { tenant_id, route_id, intent: { cost_cap: \"string|tokens\", latency_ms: number, fidelity_hint: string }, request_profile: { seq_len_estimate, kv_cache_hit: bool }, policy_version: optional }
- Response: { decision_id, fidelity_tier, variant_id, estimated_cost_tokens, cost_confidence, reasoning_trace }

POST /v1/negotiations/decide
- Purpose: real-time decision for router.
- Body: same as simulate plus request_signature and sdk_client_metadata.
- Response: decision proto + signature header. TTL on decisions: 30s by default.

GET /v1/negotiations/decisions/{decision_id}
- Purpose: debug/trace lookup. Returns recorded decision and the policy snapshot used.

Contract notes: 1) All responses include decision_id and policy_version. 2) Signing keys rotate monthly; runtime must reject unsigned or stale-signed decisions. 3) SDKs will provide a local fallback policy to use if the control plane is unreachable.
telemetry:
Required telemetry events and fields (all emitted to tracing and to metrics):

1) negotiation.request (tags: tenant_id, route_id, policy_version, intent_type, request_profile_summary)
2) negotiation.decision (tags: decision_id, fidelity_tier, variant_id, estimated_cost_tokens, cost_confidence, reason_codes)
3) negotiation.cache_hit (tags: decision_id, ttl_remaining)
4) enforcement.apply (tags: router_instance, decision_id, applied_variant, enforcement_latency_ms, fallback_flag)
5) billing.simulation_delta (tags: tenant_id, route_id, simulated_cost, actual_cost, delta_percent)

Span relationships: negotiation.request -> negotiation.decision -> enforcement.apply. Each decision_id MUST be present as a trace tag in downstream model-serving spans to enable attribution. Metrics: per-tenant cost_estimate_error histogram, negotiation_decision_latency histogram, enforcement_apply_latency. SLO alerts: p99 negotiation_decision_latency >100ms, cost_estimate_error >5% for top-100 tenants.
rollout_plan:
Phased rollout:

1) Internal lab (2 weeks): unit and integration tests, simulator agreement tests with synthetic tenants.
2) Alpha (4 weeks): select engineering tenants (3), enable simulate endpoint and offline reconciliation. Monitor cost delta and decision latency.
3) Canary (6 weeks): 5% of production tenants; enable live decide endpoint with guardrail that forces high-fidelity for a random sample of decisions (audit).
4) Gradual ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 8 weeks, gating on: p99 decision latency, billing reconciliation, and error budget consumption.

Operational gates to close before each ramp step:
- Telemetry coverage above 99% for decision_id tagging.
- Billing reconciliation error <2% for top-10 tenants.
- Security sign-off for signed decisions and key rotation.

Rollout owner: Product (Asha Patel) with Engineering owners: runtime-routing (Ravi Gupta), control-plane (Sofia Martinez).
migration_and_deprecation:
Migration guidance for existing customers:

- Default behavior: tenants are initially opted-out; Console exposes 'Enable DFCN' toggle per-tenant. When enabled, existing route-level fidelity settings are imported into the policy compiler as tenant overrides.
- Backwards compatibility: if DFCN is disabled, router continues to use legacy static route config. Decision API returns a transparent header 'X-DFCN-Enabled: false'.
- Deprecation plan: after 12 months of full adoption targets and successful reconciliation, we will deprecate legacy per-route ad-hoc flags in favor of DFCN-managed policies. Deprecation steps: communication (3 months), automatic import tool (2 months), migration window (6 months), hard-removal.
ownership_and_metrics:
Primary owners:
- Product: Asha Patel (feature roadmap, canary gating)
- Control-plane: Sofia Martinez (policy compiler, signing, simulator)
- Runtime & Router: Ravi Gupta (enforcer, low-latency cache)

Key success metrics (monthly):
- Adoption: % of eligible tenants with DFCN enabled (target 40% in first 6 months).
- Cost savings: aggregate estimated token-cost delta vs baseline for enabled tenants.
- Reliability: negotiation_decision_latency p99 <100ms and availability >99.95%.
- Accuracy: billing reconciliation delta median <2% for top-50 tenants.
- Quality regressions: number of fidelity-related customer tickets (target <5/month post 3-month ramp).
security_considerations:
- Decisions are control-plane signed with KMS-backed keys; runtime verifies signatures.
- Policy blobs can contain sensitive customer preferences; store in encrypted config store with tenant-scoped ACLs.
- Enterprise override flow requires admin-level RBAC and audit logs.
- Simulator endpoint must not be used to infer other tenants' policies; rate-limit and require auth scopes.
- Threat model: a compromised signing key could force low-fidelity defaults; mitigations include key rotation, multi-signer root, and emergency revoke with a conservative runtime quarantine policy.

SDK fallback pseudocode:

if control_plane_unavailable() then
  use_local_policy(tenant_defaults)
else
  call /v1/negotiations/decide and apply decision
end
faq: Q: Will DFCN change per-token billing? A: No; DFCN recommends and enforces model variants and quantization choices. Billing is calculated by runtime usage; we will provide simulation to estimate billing impact prior to enabling DFCN.
Q: Can customers lock a route to high-fidelity? A: Yes; tenant policies support hard locks that override negotiation intent (requires enterprise entitlements).

Q: How do we measure fidelity regressions? A: We rely on shadow-eval prompt sets and a fidelity-smoke detector that triggers if an objective score (e.g., BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim) drops beyond configured thresholds.
